newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Aug 5.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Aug 5.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

DUESSELDORF - More than every tenth mark spent on advertising goes toward promotional goods. The Association of Promotional Goods says turnover for 1997 will reach six billion marks ($3.2 billion), up from 5.7 billion marks in 1996. (Handelsblatt)
DUESSELDORF - Construction sites and building facades are becoming important new backdrops for advertising in Germany. (Handelsblatt)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

MUNICH - Television group ProSieben Media AG says it expects stable but slower growth in the German television advertising market. "We are seeing growth, but we are also seeing extreme growth in competition," ProSieben board member and marketing director Michael Woelfle says. (Reuter)
DUESSELDORF - A poll of 10 computer publishing companies shows 2.1 million Germans use online services and two-thirds of those customers are also surfing the Internet. (Handelsblatt)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

FRANKFURT - West Germany will prove the main engine for growth in Germany's job market in 1997, analysts say in a Reuters poll, giving the first upbeat assessment on the jobs outlook so far this year. (Reuter)
BONN - Volkswagen AG is again at odds with the European Union over plant subsidies, rejecting European Commission demands that it repay grants received from the state of Saxony. (Reuter)
DARMSTADT - Chemicals and drugs group Merck KGaA says it has signed a contract transferring the exclusive rights for the marketing of a generic ulcers drug to Novopharm. (Reuter) *********

BONN - Deutsche Telekom AG confirms it has lost national airline Lufthansa AG as a phone customer. Confirming a report in newsweekly Focus, Telekom says Lufthansa is switching over to Viag Interkom GmbH, a telecommunications venture between utility Viag AG and British Telecommunications Plc. (Reuter)

BONN - Industrial production rose 1.4 percent in June from May, the Economics Ministry says, in line with economists' expectations. Private-sector analysts say the data are consistent with forecasts of 2.0 to 2.5 percent economic expansion this year and could leave room for the Bundesbank to nudge interest rates higher soon if the mark continues to weaken. (Reuter)

WIESBADEN - Germans drank less German beer in the first half of the year compared with the same period a year ago, the Federal Statistics Office says. German breweries sold 55.1 million hectolitres between January and June of this year, 1.6 percent less than a year ago. (Reuter)

MUNICH - The offer period for the transfer of equity to form the basis for the merger of two German banks begins amid considerable interest from retail investors. The offer is the first stage in the merger of Bayerischen Vereinsbank and Bayerischen Hypotheken-und Wechselbank, which will ultimately create Germany's second largest commercial bank. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

FRANKFURT - Neil Simpson is named global marketing director for sportswear maker Adidas, where he will develop the company's first worldwide marketing department. Simpson was previously European marketing director for Coca-Cola. (Horizont)
WALLDORF - Johannes Moskon will become executive sales director at the publishing house Droemer Knaur, Kindler und Lichtenberg in Munich on October 1. (Kress)
